reviews.body:
Thank you. The idea is right: a browser starts the drag on the draggable element. Please fix these:

1. The build fails: `actions-dom.ts:537` gives `'dragSource' is possibly 'undefined'`, because `draggables[0]` can be undefined. Read `draggables[0]` into a constant, and fall back to `source` when it is undefined. Do not use `!`.
2. Add a file to `.changes/` for this fix.
3. In the test, remove the `document` `dragstart` listener in `afterEach`, so that one test cannot see the events of another.
4. Run `pnpm build && pnpm verify` as one command, and say in the PR that the first test fails on main.

Thank you for the fix to the build error. Some items remain:
1. `verify` fails on lint (`no-unnecessary-type-assertion`). Remove `as HTMLElement` from the `dest` arguments at test lines 55 and 67.
2. Add a file to `.changes/`.
3. Remove the `dragstart` listener from `document` in `afterEach`.
4. Choose the draggable element at the drag start point, not any single draggable descendant. Use `elementFromPoint` at the start point, then `closest('[draggable="true"]')`, and keep the result only if it is inside the source. A ref that names a child of a draggable element must also start the drag on that element.
5. Rebase on `origin/main`, run `pnpm build && pnpm verify` as one command, and push.

Read the diff and the surrounding `dragElement()`. The core choice is right: a browser starts an HTML5 drag from the draggable element under the pointer, so firing on a wrapper is what made the child's listener never see it, and "several draggable descendants, leave the source alone" is a defensible tie-break rather than a guess. The third test pinning that ambiguity control is the part I would have expected to be missing. Two residual gaps in the same predicate, both about elements `source.querySelectorAll('[draggable="true"]')` cannot see. Neither is a regression against the old behaviour, so treat these as "handle or declare" rather than must-fix. **1. Embedded roots are invisible to that query.** `querySelectorAll` does not cross a shadow boundary, and this repo already has the helper for exactly this case: `embeddedRootsUnder(root)` at `adapters/realm/browser/src/dom/query.ts:140`, documented as "Every root beneath the scope that the page can read but `querySelectorAll` will not reach" (open shadow roots and same-origin frame bodies; closed and cross-origin roots are declared blind spots). A ref naming a web-component wrapper whose handle lives inside its shadow root gives `draggables.length === 0`, so `dragSource` falls back to `source` and the drag still does not start, which is the bug in #2401 one level down. Collecting candidates from `source` plus each root returned by `embeddedRootsUnder(source)` would close it and still support the same ambiguity rule (more than one candidate means "leave the source alone"). **2. Draggability is not only the attribute.** `` and `` are draggable by default with no `draggable` attribute at all, and a browser does start a drag from them. A wrapper around a single image therefore still dispatches `dragstart` on the wrapper, since the selector matches nothing. If that shape is out of scope, one sentence in the new comment would help, so the next reader knows the predicate is attribute-only by design. For reference, I checked that no existing draggability helper is being bypassed here: the only other `draggable` mention under `adapters/realm/browser/src/` is the pointer-travel note in `actions/actions-dom.ts:422`.

comments.body: Thanks for your first pull request to Reticle! A maintainer aims to review within two days. Before then, `pnpm verify` locally catches most of what CI will, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/reticlehq/reticle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) explains the rest. If CI does not start, a maintainer needs to approve it for first-time contributors; that is normal.
